# Woge application coding guidance

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-spring-boot-agent-guidance.sh from template v1 and the Woge framework index. Do not edit generated copies. -->

This file describes the supported application shape for this exact scaffold. Humans and coding agents
use the same public APIs, compiler feedback, examples and documentation.

## Version-matched baseline

- Scaffold: `spring-boot` 0.2.0
- Woge: 0.1.0-SNAPSHOT
- Kotlin: 2.4.10
- Spring Boot: 4.1.1
- Build JDK: 21; produced JVM bytecode: Java 17
- Selected host: `webflux` (Spring Boot WebFlux)
- Frontend tooling: none is required. Playwright 1.62.1 is test-only; Tailwind and Vite
  are not installed.

Run `./gradlew test` after application changes. Run `./gradlew bootRun` for the selected host. Change
`wogeSpringAdapter` in `gradle.properties` to `mvc` or `webflux` deliberately; do not mix both host
adapters in application code. Regenerate this file after changing the persisted host or a pinned
framework version; the normal test task rejects stale guidance.

## Keep the web platform visible

- Render semantic HTML on the server. Keep links, forms, methods, status codes and URLs recognizable.
- Write ordinary browser CSS in `src/main/resources/static`. String class names are intentional and
  remain compatible with plain CSS, CSS Modules and an optional later Tailwind pipeline.
- Deliver a useful native-navigation path before adding progressive enhancement. JavaScript may make a
  path faster; it must not become the only way to complete the core task.
- Keep domain and markup functions host-neutral. Spring request, response, Reactor and Servlet types
  belong only in the selected host adapter source set.

## Supported and unsupported shapes

| Concern | Use | Avoid |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typed page input | `PageUseCase<ProjectInput>` with `PageRequest<ProjectInput>` | maps of strings or a Spring request inside the page |
| Markup | Woge element functions and `text(dynamicValue)` | HTML string concatenation or unaudited `raw(...)` |
| Application URL | `applicationUrl("/projects/woge")` passed to `url(...)` | unchecked dynamic URL strings in attributes |
| Native form | `form` with normal `method`, `action`, named controls and server validation | JavaScript-only submission or duplicated native/enhanced policy |
| Region target | `PatchTarget(PageEpoch, RegionTargetId)` and `regionPlaceholder(...)` | manual CSS selectors such as `#summary` as patch identity |
| Host boundary | a small route adapter calling the portable page port | Spring, Reactor or Servlet imports in reusable components |
| CSS | external modern CSS, class strings and bounded `declarations(...)` for inline values | a Kotlin catalog that hides normal CSS or unsanitized style data |

Generated typed page/route and action references are not part of Woge 0.1.0-SNAPSHOT yet. Until their
owning APIs land, use native form/URL semantics and decode inputs at the host edge. Do not invent
`ActionRef`, route annotations or selector-based action targets. When generated descriptors become
available, prefer them over duplicated route, action and region strings.

## Safety and generated ownership

- Dynamic text goes through `text(...)`; audited sanitizer output is the only reason to opt in to
  `unsafeHtml(...)` and `raw(...)`.
- Application-local URLs use `applicationUrl(...)`; external URLs use `externalUrl(...)`. Do not bypass
  URL validation to silence the compiler.
- Treat CSS strings as CSS, not as an HTML escape hatch. Keep untrusted values out of stylesheets and
  declaration lists.
- Woge generators alone own `build/generated/sources/woge/main/kotlin`.
  Never edit or commit that directory; change source declarations and regenerate.
- Native Declarative Partial Updates remain experimental browser syntax and are not an application
  dependency. Use the supported Woge fallback behavior.
